authTierRationale: The only credential mode is a single user-generated Smartsheet API Access Token (Account > Apps & Integrations > API Access), passed straight through by the CDK's TokenSource with oauth_spec=None as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. No OAuth app registration and no refresh token are involved — the connector never calls a token endpoint for this credential type.

unionMisfits.description: The detail endpoints (GET /sheets/{id}, GET /reports/{id}) carry NO pageNumber/totalPages and silently CLAMP to the last valid page instead of erroring or returning empty. The walk therefore terminates on two conditions at once: (a) client-side arithmetic `page * pageSize >= totalRowCount` where totalRowCount is read from the response remainder, and (b) an empty page — but (b) is only trusted when no rowsModifiedSince filter is set, because the API paginates BEFORE filtering, so a filtered page can legitimately be empty mid-walk. `terminateOn` is a single enum and cannot express a conditional pair. Recorded as explicit_total because that is the always-correct bound.

The `sheets` stream is a two-hop pull that one PullSpec cannot express: the list walk over GET /sheets yields only {id, modifiedAt} summaries, and for EACH surviving summary the connector then issues GET /sheets/{id}?page=1&pageSize=1 purely to harvest the detail envelope's metadata remainder (the single embedded row is drained and discarded). The emitted document is the detail envelope, not the list item; the paginator and incrementalParam recorded belong to the list hop only.

streamMode is `static` (four fixed bindings) yet the customer's own sheet ids ARE discovered — but they become per-sheet SUB-PARTITIONS of state inside the single `sheet_rows` binding (state.inc / state.backfill keyed by sheet id), not separate streams. Discovery happens only when the binding opens; new sheets appearing between runs are patched into state at the next open. The schema has no place for intra-binding discovered partitions, so `discovery` is null and the fact lives in pathPlaceholders.

partitionDiscovery.method: GET /sheets list walk at binding open

unionMisfits.description: The incremental cursor for `sheets` is read from the LIST item (SheetSummary.modifiedAt) and clamped to `min(max modifiedAt seen, poll_start - 5min)` to absorb a measured 5-65s lag in the list's modifiedSince index. The emitted document (the detail envelope) is not what the cursor is taken from, and the schema has no field for a lag allowance or a cursor clamp.

abstained.discovery: streamMode is static — the four streams are hard-coded resources in all_resources(). The customer's sheet ids are enumerated at binding-open time, but they become state sub-partitions of the single `sheet_rows` binding rather than discovered streams, so nothing belongs in `discovery`. See unionMisfits[2].
abstained.transports[0].spec.defaultHeaders: No headers are set anywhere in the connector beyond the CDK's Authorization header; no Content-Type, Accept, or user-agent is configured.
abstained.execution.continuity: Poll-mode HTTP connector: no server-side artifacts are created on Smartsheet's side (no slots, subscriptions, webhooks, or scratch objects), all state is client-side cursors, and nothing accrues on the customer's infra between polls. Set null rather than fabricating an artifact list. Note the one non-continuity gap the code documents: `rowsModifiedSince` never surfaces blank/never-cell-written rows, which is why sheet_rows carries a daily cron re-backfill.
abstained.credentialModes[0].scheme.field (exact w: Not abstained on the mechanism (CDK sends `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`), but the connector never sets authorization_header/authorization_token_type, so the wire form comes entirely from CDK defaults rather than from anything in source-smartsheet itself.
abstained.streams[2].cursorField / streams[3].curs: Deliberately none. models.py documents that GET /reports' own `modifiedSince` reflects the report DEFINITION's modified time (rename/recolumn/create), not the underlying sheet data a report renders, and there is no per-report version endpoint to fall back on — hence full snapshot replication with tombstones.
